To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of consistency enforcement techniques, variable/value ordering heutistics, and intelligent look-back schemes can improve the effectiveness of a depth-first backtracking procedure for solving the job shop scheduling constraint satisfaction problem.

(1) a combination of variable ordering heuristics and consistency enforcing techniques can significantly reduce the average computational cost of a depth-first backtrack search procedure for the job shop scheduling CSP and (2) the combination of these techniques with three look-back schemes can further improve the efficiency of the search procedure and make the system more robust.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in addition to improving the efficiency of the search procedure by enforcing higher consistency levels among variables and using more intelligent variable ordering heuristics, the search procedure can be further improved by using “intelligent” look-back schemes that enable it to recover from deadend search states and avoid excessive computation costs.
the use of backtracking techniques is a promising direction for solving the job shop scheduling CSP.
